transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

I’ve been thinking about death a lot lately and wondering if my family would be better off without me. My daughter got really worried when I told her about it, and she's the one who insisted on bringing me in today.
Have you been having thoughts of harming yourself or ending your life?

Yes, I have... Every night when I lie down, I find myself thinking it wouldn't be so bad if I just didn't wake up. I've even caught myself picturing ways I could make that happen so my husband and kids wouldn't have to deal with me dragging them down anymore.
Have you had periods like this before, or is this the first time you've felt this way?

Looking back, these swings between feeling wound-up and then sinking into these dark, heavy depressions have been coming and going for at least a year. It has really ramped up and gotten much worse since I started cutting back my work hours.
Have there been times when you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or were more talkative or impulsive than usual?

Yes, a few weeks ago I felt incredibly wired and touchy, talking a mile a minute and waking up before dawn to frantically clean and reorganize because I couldn't sit still. My thoughts were racing so fast I couldn't sleep, and I even almost threw a huge chunk of our savings into an online eco-housing project before my daughter stopped me. It's really embarrassing to look back on how wound-up and impulsive I was during that stretch.

The presence of distinct past (hypo)manic episodes, including increased energy, decreased need for sleep, racing thoughts, impulsivity, and pressured speech, confirms a bipolar disorder diagnosis.
